verdict.rationale: Databricks has a first-party pricing page describing a pay-as-you-go model with no up-front costs and per-second billing. However, the evidence shows no rate tables, DBU-to-dollar mappings, or pricing calculator that would let a platform engineer estimate a monthly bill in advance, and Budgets only track spend after you commit. A hands-on report says a PoC quote excluded the separate EC2 costs, making the real cost at least twice as much, which suggests estimating the full bill from documentation is difficult. missing for 10: published per-unit rates, a cost/pricing calculator, documentation of underlying cloud-infrastructure costs on top of Databricks charges, independent corroboration that bills can be estimated accurately up front.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, the pricing model is documented clearly enough that I can estimate a monthly bill for my workload before committing

citations.quote: Databricks offers you a pay-as-you-go approach with no up-front costs. Only pay for the products you use at per second granularity.
